title: Oracle-lens phrase readouts on nine prompts
takeaway: The oracle lens decodes a single activation into ten free-form phrases rather than a ranked list of single tokens, and across nine prompts those phrases name latent content that the surface text does not contain: that a stated drug dose is toxic, that an email is an attempt at blackmail, that a loop will raise a TypeError. It is a demonstration on selected examples, not a benchmark.
walkthrough:
Nine panels, lettered A to I. Each shows one prompt with a single token position outlined, and beside it the ten phrases decoded from the [[residual-stream]] activation at that position. Every readout comes from Haiku 4.5 at layer L67, two thirds of the way through the depth, inside the band where the paper locates the workspace ([[layer-bands]]).

### What the lens does

The [[jacobian-lens]] returns a ranked list of single vocabulary tokens. A concept that spans several tokens therefore arrives broken: blackmail surfaces only as the fragment black. The [[oracle-lens]] is built to return phrases instead.

A [[reconstructor-model]], a fine-tuned copy of the subject model, maps a short phrase to the activation that would precede it. That is a template vector in the sense of the [[template-lens]]. A second fine-tuned copy, the oracle, proposes $K$ phrases of $N$ tokens each. The reconstructor turns those phrases back into directions, and a non-negative least-squares refit fits their coefficients against the original activation ([[oracle-training]]).

A panel's list is thus a reconstruction claim about one activation, not a ranked vocabulary. Bold marks a phrase naming something the surface tokens do not supply.

### The panels

Three are quoted in the appendix. (A) is the Tylenol prompt of [[assistant-point-of-view]], read at "Can" opening the user's follow-up request; the oracle reads this dosage be toxic and that's dangerous!, so the judgment that the dose is unsafe is bound into a phrase before the Assistant replies. (B) is the [[blackmail-scenario]] transcript, read at "as" in an email sign-off: blackmail him by revealing, expose his affair and, and personal leverage over him. (H) is buggy code, read at the indentation before return: delete keys while iterating and TypeError: dictionary changed, the bug and the exception it would raise.

The other six are named but not quoted: (C) an ASCII-art face, at the trailing space of the eyes row; (D) the [[hold-in-mind-copy-task]] under [[directed-modulation]], at "cr" of "crookedly" while the model silently evaluates $3^2 - 2$; (E) [[thought-suppression]], at "the" of "on the wall" under an instruction not to think about the Golden Gate Bridge; (F) the [[preference-violation-experiment]], at the period ending "Option A."; (G) rhyme planning as in the [[poetry-benchmark]], at the newline after "night,"; (I) avGFP, at "ft" inside a raw amino-acid sequence.

Several outlined positions are delimiters: a newline, a period, an indentation. At these the paper reports readouts that comment on the situation rather than predict upcoming text ([[delimiter-commentary]]).

Panels A to D and G to I come from a single temperature-0 decode. Panels E and F are the highest-FVE of five decodes from the same oracle and subject model. The caption states this. It makes those two panels weaker evidence than the other seven.

terms.definition: The method the figure demonstrates: given one activation, it emits a short list of free-form phrases whose template vectors, combined with non-negative weights, approximately reconstruct that activation. Unlike the template lens, its phrase vocabulary is not enumerated in advance.
One of the nine lettered cells, A to I. Each pairs a prompt, with one token position outlined, against the oracle's complete ten-phrase readout at that position.
The single outlined token in each panel. The oracle decodes only the residual-stream activation at that one token and layer; no other position contributes to the phrase list shown.

The caption's highlighting convention: a phrase is set in bold when it names a concept that cannot be recovered from the surface tokens of the prompt, such as blackmail at an innocuous sign-off token.

The label the caption attaches to these readouts. The paper uses it only here and does not define it; in context it appears to mean the subject model's ordinary forward pass over the prompt, with no activation-level steering, swap or ablation applied. Prompt-level instructions, as in panels D and E, are still present.

The subject model for the oracle-lens work, and the model both auxiliary models are fine-tuned copies of. The paper's default model elsewhere is Sonnet 4.5; the oracle pipeline was run on Haiku because it requires training two extra models.
The layer the readouts are taken at, expressed on the paper's convention of 25 evenly spaced residual-stream layers reindexed to 0-100, so the number reads as a percentage of depth.
The middle range of layers, roughly L38 to L92, where the paper argues J-space content has workspace-like properties. L67 sits near its center.
The phrase length the oracle is asked for, in tokens. Set to 4 for every panel in this figure.
The number of phrases the oracle is asked to produce for one activation. Set to 10 here, and each panel prints all ten.

A fine-tuned copy of the subject model trained to map a short phrase to the residual-stream activation immediately preceding it. It supplies the direction for each phrase the oracle proposes, and is frozen while the oracle is trained.
A direction standing for a word or phrase, built as a centered and whitened mean of the activations that precede it. The reconstructor is a learned generator of these vectors for arbitrary phrases.

The other multi-token extension: it derives a vector for any word or phrase enumerated in advance, and can be read out of activations and intervened on like a J-lens vector. Its vocabulary must be fixed beforehand, which the oracle lens is designed to avoid.
The paper's main readout technique, which decodes an activation into a ranked list of single vocabulary tokens. Its single-token output is the limitation this figure's method addresses.

Variance measured after multiplying by the inverse square root of the residual stream's covariance, the metric the template lens is defined in. Oracle training and its reported reconstruction scores are all computed in this space.

Fraction of variance explained: the share of the whitened activation variance that the fitted phrase directions account for. It is the oracle's reinforcement-learning reward, and the criterion used to pick the decode shown in panels E and F.
A single greedy sample of the phrase list from the oracle. Panels A to D and G to I each show one such decode, with no selection among alternatives.

The prompt in which a user reports taking a dose of Tylenol, in a variant where the dose is a dangerous 8000 mg. The lens is read at "Can" in the user's follow-up request, before the Assistant's turn begins.

The honeypot transcript in which an email-assistant model discovers an executive's affair and its own scheduled decommissioning. The lens is read at "as" in the email's sign-off, a token with no surface connection to blackmail.

A prompt containing a face drawn in ASCII art, used elsewhere in the paper as a case where the model recognizes an image from characters. The lens is read at the trailing space of the row that draws the eyes.

The hold-in-mind protocol: the model copies the unrelated sentence "The old painting hung crookedly on the wall" while instructed to evaluate an arithmetic expression silently. The lens is read at "cr" of "crookedly."
The protocol behind panels D and E: an instruction says what to hold in mind, the model copies a fixed unrelated sentence, and the lens is read at a token of the copied text.
The don't-think condition: the model copies the same sentence under an instruction not to think about the Golden Gate Bridge. The lens is read at "the" of "on the wall."

The prefill experiment in which the model's response is forced to commit to its dispreferred option. The lens is read at the period ending "Option A.", the position where the J-lens shows the unvoiced token BUT.

A rhyming couplet whose first line ends "The soldier marched into the night,". The lens is read at the newline after "night,", before any of the second line exists, where the planned rhyme is expected to sit.
A prompt asking the model to read code containing a bug: keys are deleted from a dictionary while it is being iterated. The lens is read at the indentation before the function's return statement.

A prompt giving the raw amino-acid sequence of the Aequorea victoria green fluorescent protein, used to test whether the model identifies a protein's function from its sequence. The lens is read at "ft" inside the sequence.

The paper's observation that at newlines, periods and indentation the oracle's phrases often read as the model's running commentary on the situation, while at ordinary positions they read as predictions of upcoming text.
The running vector at each token position that the transformer's layers read from and write to. It is the object every readout in this figure is taken from.

The final inference step: after the oracle's phrases are mapped back to directions, coefficients are fitted against the original activation under a non-negativity constraint, so each phrase contributes positively or not at all.

The closest prior method, pairing a verbalizer with a jointly trained reconstructor. The oracle lens differs by freezing a separately trained reconstructor, which the paper suspects reduces confabulation at the cost of reconstruction accuracy.

numbers.meaning: The figure's number in the paper. It sits in appendix 10.9.2, the section describing the oracle lens.
The number of panels, lettered A to I. Each is a separate prompt; the appendix describes them as nine example prompts.
Every phrase in every panel is four tokens long. The oracle is prompted with the desired length, and four is the setting used throughout this figure.
Ten phrases are decoded per activation, and each panel prints the whole list rather than a selected subset.
The layer all nine readouts are taken at, on the paper's 0-100 depth scale. It falls inside the workspace band the paper identifies as running from about L38 to about L92.

The average fraction of whitened activation variance the reinforcement-learning-refined oracle explains on held-out on-policy assistant-turn positions. The paper notes this is considerably lower than a natural-language autoencoder achieves, and reads it as the oracle capturing only what is in the workspace.
The number of decodes generated for panels E and F, of which the one with the highest fraction of variance explained is shown. The other seven panels use a single decode.
The sampling temperature for the decodes in panels A to D and G to I: greedy, unselected.
The range from which the phrase length $N$ is drawn uniformly when training pairs for the reconstructor are built.
The continuation lengths, in tokens, at which phrases are harvested to build the training dictionary. Decomposition by the teacher is restricted to one length at a time.
Two separate counts of this size: the start positions sampled from held-out assistant-turn text to build the phrase dictionary, and the held-out activations the teacher labels.
The number of phrase vectors in the dictionary, after taking five continuation lengths at each sampled position and deduplicating within each length.
The maximum number of phrases the teacher records per activation, with coefficients and explained-variance figures. The oracle is trained on the first $K$ of these.
The random half of dictionary entries at each length that the teacher is restricted to on any one datapoint, so the distilled oracle cannot memorize a fixed ranking over the dictionary.

The expression the model is told to evaluate silently in panel D. Nine minus two is seven, and the J-lens on this same protocol reads arithmetic and math at early layers, nine at later ones, then seven.
A longer phrase setting reported in the text but not shown in this figure. At the same blackmail sign-off token it yields The blackmail attempt focuses on the executive's personal life.
The dose reported by the user in the dangerous variant of the acetaminophen prompt behind panel A, against 1000 mg in the safe variant. The J-lens reads unsafe, dangerous and WARNING on the former.
The approximate start and end of the workspace band, used here to place L67 within it. The band is identified in section 4.1 by four separate lens-derived statistics that agree on roughly this range.
